prompt: A rider on a Ferris wheel is at height $h(t) = 20 + 18\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{15}\right)$ metres after $t$ seconds. At what height, in metres, is the centre of the wheel?
hint: The rider circles evenly around the centre of the wheel, so the centre sits on the midline of the graph.

hints.text: The rider circles evenly around the centre of the wheel, so the centre sits on the midline of the graph.
The midline of $y = D + A\sin(\ldots)$ is $y = D$.
Here $D = 20$, so the centre is $20$ metres up.

explanation: The sine part swings between $-18$ and $18$, averaging out to zero.
What is left is the constant $20$, which is the midline of the motion.
The rider is always $18$ m from that line, so the centre of the wheel is $20$ m above the ground.

alternativeExplanations.title: Average the top and the bottom
steps: Highest point: $20 + 18 = 38$ m. Lowest point: $20 - 18 = 2$ m.
The centre is halfway between: $\frac{38 + 2}{2} = 20$ m.
